voiceover: In Mark's Gospel, the first human being to confess that Jesus is the Son of God is a Roman officer — and what moves him, on Mark's telling, is above all the manner of a death. And when the centurion, who stood facing him, saw that in this way he breathed his last, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God! That is a strange place to look for God. In the ancient world a crucified man was the opposite of divine: a slave's death, a rebel's death, and to a Jew a death under the curse of the Law. Yet the Philippians hymn, widely regarded as older than Paul's letter, tells of one who was already in the form of God, and places his death on a cross on the path to the name above every name. And in Revelation, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, is worshipped with the one on the throne. The figure who shares the worship of the Creator is the slaughtered one. The Son of God, who is truly God, truly died on the cross, in the human nature he had taken to himself. The divine nature did not die, and the Father was not crucified. So the cross discloses not that God is mortal, but what kind of love God is: not a power that saves itself, but a love that gives itself. The word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

scenes.vo: In Mark's Gospel, the first human being to confess that Jesus is the Son of God is a Roman officer — and what moves him, on Mark's telling, is above all the manner of a death.
And when the centurion, who stood facing him, saw that in this way he breathed his last, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God!
That is a strange place to look for God. In the ancient world a crucified man was the opposite of divine: a slave's death, a rebel's death, and to a Jew a death under the curse of the Law.
Yet the Philippians hymn, widely regarded as older than Paul's letter, tells of one who was already in the form of God, and places his death on a cross on the path to the name above every name.
And in Revelation, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, is worshipped with the one on the throne. The figure who shares the worship of the Creator is the slaughtered one.
The Son of God, who is truly God, truly died on the cross, in the human nature he had taken to himself. The divine nature did not die, and the Father was not crucified.
So the cross discloses not that God is mortal, but what kind of love God is: not a power that saves itself, but a love that gives itself.
The word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
